issue.description:
Child of beadrs-b722358e (umbrella), after beadrs-3d97a9c4. Settle what the versioned naming scheme is and exactly which artifact/commit this pin targets.

Acceptance:
- Confirm the repo scheme <name>-<shaslice> from the existing pins (bead-attempt-resolution-e115609, bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c) and the scheme statements in pinned-binaries/README.md and COMMITS.md
- Identify the exact source binary and commit SHA this pin targets: current HEAD pin is bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c, git_commit_sha f25ab5c91c09a3408f23b9cdf2f3e95e81abc060, verified against its metadata.json and commits.json/COMMITS.md
- Contrast with the ~/.cargo/bin variant scheme (<name>-v<semver>) documented by beadrs-3d97a9c4 and state which scheme downstream pin children must follow
- Write the scheme statement and target identity as a single unambiguous verdict, citing the files each fact came from
issue.notes:
VERDICT (naming scheme + pin target):

SCHEME — The repo pin scheme is <name>-<shaslice>: role stem (<name>, e.g. attempt-resolution) + first 7 hex chars of the source commit full SHA. Stated verbatim at pinned-binaries/README.md:16 ("**Naming scheme:** <name>-<shaslice> ... first 7 hex characters of the source commit"). Confirmed by both shaslice pins: bead-attempt-resolution-e115609 <-> git_commit_short "e115609" of e1156098b01264bb998797047115521261443c13, and bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c <-> "f25ab5c" of f25ab5c91c09a3408f23b9cdf2f3e95e81abc060 (each pin own *.metadata.json git_commit_short; same values in commits.json and the COMMITS.md "Short SHA" fields). The two role-only baselines (bead-pre-feature, bead-pre-attempt-resolution) predate the convention and are explicitly grandfathered (README.md:16); their commits live in metadata + COMMITS.md, not their names.

TARGET — The current HEAD pin is pinned-binaries/bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c and targets source commit f25ab5c91c09a3408f23b9cdf2f3e95e81abc060 ("docs(attempts-binary): add comprehensive build process and verification documentation", 2026-09-02). Verified four independent ways this session: (1) bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c.metadata.json fields git_commit_sha/git_commit_short/git_commit_message; (2) commits.json attempt_resolution_f25ab5c.full_sha; (3) COMMITS.md "Current HEAD Binary (Pinned)" section; (4) the artifact itself, live: sha256 9a8455f25bacf5bc961bd740442fdc1b30a67fb6e38d304c23c97a57cf57b04e (== metadata binary_sha256 == README hash table), --version "bead 0.2.6 (f25ab5c-dirty 2026-09-02T10:52:25Z)" (== embedded_version_string), size 7,305,184 B (== binary_size_bytes). f25ab5c is an ancestor of current git HEAD 7d08577; "HEAD pin" means HEAD-of-record at pin time (the pin artifact + metadata were committed after f25ab5c: Bin 0 -> 7305184 across f25ab5c..HEAD). Rebuild caveat stands: the hash is NOT reproducible (build.rs re-embeds the build timestamp), so verify by sha256 against metadata.json, never by rebuilding.

TWIN-LINEAGE FOOTNOTE — commit 63c2ee8 message says "pin HEAD attempt-resolution binary at b0d7840". b0d7840 is tree-identical to f25ab5c (git diff empty): the same commit on the force-pushed twin lineage, reconciled by merge 7d08577. Every record of record (metadata.json, commits.json, COMMITS.md, README.md, and the binary own embedded version string) identifies f25ab5c, so f25ab5c is the canonical identifier; b0d7840 is an alias of the same tree and names no separate artifact. Downstream children citing the pin must use f25ab5c91c09a3408f23b9cdf2f3e95e81abc060.

CONTRAST (~/.cargo/bin) — Per beadrs-3d97a9c4 notes: the installed-variant scheme is <role>-v<semver> (bead-pre-resolution-v0.1.3, bead-with-resolution-v0.2.0): version-labeled, no sha component, and the version labels are demonstrably stale (0/3 filename versions equal the embedded version; bead-pre-resolution-v0.1.3 embeds 0.2.6/946a727-dirty). Role wording diverges too (pre-resolution/with-resolution vs pre-attempt-resolution/attempt-resolution-<sha>). The two schemes share zero names; the one real correspondence (variant 2 <-> bead-pre-attempt-resolution, same commit+size) is discoverable only by commit/size comparison, and even that file is a dirty rebuild, not a byte-copy of the pin.

RULE FOR DOWNSTREAM PIN CHILDREN — Follow the repo scheme <name>-<shaslice>: name the artifact attempt-resolution-<first-7-hex-of-source-commit>, commit it under pinned-binaries/ alongside a <name>.metadata.json recording the full git_commit_sha and binary_sha256, add its row to the README pin-inventory table (README.md says the table is maintained against ls pinned-binaries/ — verified accurate this session: exactly the four pins listed, everything else docs/metadata). Never use the <role>-v<semver> form: that scheme belongs to ~/.cargo/bin installed variants and its version labels are unreliable by construction. Pin the staged bytes; do not rebuild and expect the hash to reproduce.

issue.description:
ADR-005 (Accepted, 2026-08-16) decisions that an `open` issue carrying an assignee is not a claim but is excluded from the ready frontier, and nothing currently surfaces that shape — `show` and `doctor` report it as healthy. Field precedent: 583 stuck issues across 47 of 66 workspaces, ten with an entirely empty frontier while workers starved. Add an advisory `ready_frontier` check under doctor's `dependencies` scope that warns when open issues carry an assignee, names a bounded sample of the offending ids, and states the exact remedy (`bead update <id> --clear-assignee`). Advisory only: doctor never clears an assignee, not even under `--repair` (diagnose-don't-mutate per plan section 7 and the R034 posture). No open bead covers this. Verification: synthetic workspace with assigned-open issues produces the warning with ids and remedy; assigned `in_progress` and deliberately parked cases behave per the ADR's documented tradeoff; `doctor --repair` provably leaves assignment state untouched.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Add a doctor ready_frontier check diagnosing open issues held off the frontier by assignment
